A1.justification: Despite the changed title and reorganized appendices, both PDFs describe the same interpretability study. The text, equations, figures, table, and appendices are readable and support reliable matching of retained and added material.

before.justification: V1 reports original training, probe, activation-analysis, and mask-patching results on CHES_CTF, ESHARD, and ASCAD in Section 5 and Appendices C-F.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds gradient visualizations and an ASCAD CNN analysis, including new empirical plots in Appendices A and G.

M1.justification: The output-logit analysis, principal-component analysis, and activation-patching procedure remain unchanged between v1 Section 4 and v2 Section 3. The CNN addition tests the existing analysis on another architecture.

E1.justification: Both versions use CHES_CTF power traces, ESHARD electromagnetic traces, and variable-key ASCAD electromagnetic traces from masked AES-128 implementations. The added CNN and gradient analyses reuse this coverage; other ciphers and masking schemes are discussed but not tested.

E2.justification: V1 only discusses input-attribution methods. V2 Appendix A and Figure 8 add gradient-based visualizations for the three existing MLPs and qualitatively compare their highlighted regions with leakage identified through recovered shares.

E3.justification: Existing dataset splits, preprocessing, and MLP training settings remain unchanged. The added CNN experiment examines the final model at epoch 100 and representations after the third convolutional block; the gradient comparison also introduces checkpoint-specific attribution evaluations.

E4.justification: V2 adds a targeted architecture-generalization case study on ASCAD using CNN probes, representations, and logits, plus gradient-visualization checks on the existing MLPs. Earlier activation-patching experiments and ASCAD bitwise controls are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. The added plots do not introduce an uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: All original result plots and Table 1 values are retained, including ASCAD probe accuracy 0.64, PI 2.47 versus 2.58, and entropy 0.27 bits. New results concern gradient maps and CNN learning, representations, and logits. The CNN component assignments are inconsistent: Appendix G gives input/output pairs 0/2 and 1/3, while Figure 14 labels them 0/3 and 1/2.

T1.justification: The Hamming-weight recombination analysis, parity identity, and 16-class ASCAD construction are retained from v1 Appendices E-F in v2 Appendices H-I. Background rewriting introduces no substantive new formal assumptions, derivations, or proofs.

C1.justification: Both versions claim that mechanistic interpretability can explain successful side-channel models without prior mask knowledge, recover secret shares, and reveal recurring representations across targets. The new title and emphasis on sudden performance jumps preserve the substance of these contributions.

C2.justification: V2 substantially expands applicability limits: structured data, few relevant features, limited relevance to larger models, and dependence on domain expertise. Sections 5-6 also add interpretations about sequential feature refinement, possible cross-cipher transfer, prime-field masking defenses, and practical barriers to automated evaluation.

D1.justification: V2 adds a reproduction-code URL and Appendix D documenting 64 GB RAM, an NVIDIA 4080 GPU, training under an hour, and comparable time for PI/probe plots. Existing dataset-processing instructions and MLP hyperparameters remain unchanged.

R1.justification: New Appendix A expands brief SCA positioning into substantive comparisons with input attribution, layer analyses, and interpretable architectures, adding works such as Kilroy Was Here, Wu et al.'s ablation analysis, and OccPoIs. V2 also adds superposition, sparse-autoencoder, masking, and Transformer context while removing the output-centric interpretability citation.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, background, and discussion are extensively rewritten. Separate SCA and mechanistic-interpretability sections become a combined Background section; later sections and appendices are reorganized, the Impact Statement is removed, and acknowledgments are added.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from two-column to single-column layout, with substantial figure repositioning and text wrapping. New Figures 2, 8, 13, 14, and 18 add a trace illustration, gradient visualizations, and CNN plots; the original result figures and Table 1 remain.

improvement.justification: V2 tests the CNN extension that v1 only suggested, adds a useful qualitative attribution comparison, and improves scope qualifications and reproducibility documentation. These are limited gains because the central evidence and incomplete ASCAD mask recovery remain unchanged. The new inconsistency between Appendix G's component assignments and Figure 14 also reduces the precision of the added CNN analysis.
